pr_title: drivers: flash: flash_stm32g4x.c: manage bank1/2 discontinuity
pr_body:
drivers: flash: flash_stm32g4x.c: manage bank1/2 discontinuity

When flash is Dualbank and flash size is lower than 512K,
then there is a discontinutity between bank1 and bank2.

Fixes #30148
pr_comments: @Laczen @nvlsianpu, with your flash experience, can you please comment this proposal to manage discontinuity between bank1 and bank2 ?

Just tested this code on G474RCT and observed the below thing.

When I flash the code in Bank 2 (0x08040000) and write to the offset 0x5F800, it fails occasionally giving me a flash_write failure (err:-5). This happens only from Bank 2.

Can this be related to the below PR? 
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/29792

I also tested few other cases, which seems to be working fine. So,

App in Bank 2 (0x08040000),  write to 0x5F800 => Gives the above issue
App in Bank 2 (0x08040000),  write to 0x1F800 => OK
App in Bank 1 (0x08000000),  write to 0x5F800 => OK
App in Bank 1 (0x08000000),  write to 0x1F800 => OK

Hi @azeemshatp,
I could not reproduce your issue because I don't have soc stm32g474rct (I only have nucleo_g474re) and because I face difficulties to run application on 2nd bank.
Nevertheless I found some hardcoded page limit value in erase code, which for sure don't match with smaller flash size like you have on stm32g474rct.
So I pushed a 2nd commit on this PR.
Even if I didn't found the link with the fact that you face issue only when erasing this specific address 0x5F800 from bank2,
I still hope this fixes the issue.
It works on my nucleo_g474re, but I couldn't test on stm32g474rct.
Could you test this new commit ? 
I would be interested by tests at address:
* 0x0805F800 from bank2 (the case which cause issue)
* 0x08020000 should failed as invalid address (between bank1 and bank2)

As erase operation is concerned, I propose you to update tests as follow, for each address
```
flash_erase();
flash_write();
flash_read();  // so that we can check write operation is effective
flash_erase();
flash_read(); // so that we can check erase operation is effective
```

Note: in case this doesn't fix your problem can you please enable switch FLASH_LOG_LEVEL_DBG and provide the log.

If the case is similar for STM32G474, then after a bank switch, I think the address 0x08000000 becomes the base address of Bank 2 and for the Bank 1, the base address should be 0x08040000.

I think I got the point:
The driver is not designed to tackle bank swap.
This concerns only erase operation as it is necessary to select the bank (for read and write there is no bank selection).
Currently bank selection is based on offset: (offset > 0x40000) ==> select bank2 
But with a bank swap it is not valid. selection should be inverted.
For test purpose you can try to invert lines 119 and 124 of file drivers/flash/flash_stm32g4x.c 
I hope it works, but only for boot from bank2.
I will investigate further on monday how to make it work whatever bank is booted.

Ya, that seems to be the case. The driver doesn't handle the address remapping correctly. As you mentioned, inverting the lines 119 and 124 seem to work for Bank 2. Looking forward to an update next week. Thanks a lot

issue_context.title: STM32G474: Write to flash Bank 2 address 0x08040000 does not work in 256K flash version
comments:
Hi @azeemshatp,
It is working fine on my side (with default partition settings)
* with flash_shell sample (without changes)
* with your code (original post) in condition to activate switch MPU_ALLOW_FLASH_WRITE
  i.e. same solution that for #29796

Because flash_shell sample activate this switch, it may explain it is working when you use flah_shell sample.
Can you check the same?

> 2. It doesnt make sense to me in G474 with only 128K size for each bank, how did it even allow me to successfully write to and read from the flash offset 0x20000.

G474 in dualbank configuration has 2 bank of 128 pages, with 2K pages. So 1st bank ends at 0x3FFFF. So 0x20000 is part of bank1

MPU_ALLOW_FLASH_WRITE was already activated in my case.

Regarding the point 2: 
May be I am missing something here. 
I am using STM32G474RCT, which is a 256K flash version. So this can only have a single bank size of 128K max. So if we consider 2k sized pages in dual bank mode, there could only be 64 pages per bank, or not?
Just noticed that the nucleo board where I found the code was working fine, has the MCU STM32G474RET, which is a 512K flash version. So the issue seems to be only with the 256K version.

> I am using STM32G474RCT,

Ok, as it was not specified, I was supposing you used  nucleo_g474re which is supported in zephyr.
So now, knowing that it seems you can write to address 0x08020000 and not at  0x08040000,
maybe you are in single bank configuration.
Can you check the value of option byte  DBANK ?Aand make sure it is set to 1.

The value of option byte DBANK was 1 already. However, I also had the options nSWBOOT0=0 and nBOOT0=1, for hardware specific reasons.

Just another note:
In the 256k version, I was able to write manually to the Bank 2 (Address 0x08040000) correctly using STM32CubeProgrammer. So the Bank 2 address seems to be correct. But writing using the Zephyr API is what gave me the error.

So with the dualbank configuration on STM32G474RCT,
there is a discontinuity between bank1 and bank2 (0x08020000 -- 0x0803FFFF is physically not accesssible).
Unfortunately, it seems STM32G4 flash driver is not able to tackle this discontinuity, specially when creating flash layout.
In other word it assumes that bank2 is contigiuous to bank1, which explain why you cannot write at 0x08040000.
I will check whether we can trick the driver to make it work.

Also looking into this a bit. It seems like the issue is even beyond the STM32G4 implementation. The `struct flash_pages_layout` only contains the number of pages and their size, but no offset. So even if `flash_stm32_page_layout` in the `flash_stm32g4x.c` returned a separate layout for each bank, the function `flash_get_page_info` would not be able to know about the gap in the flash layout.

A very dirty trick to make it work is to just multiply the pages count by a factor of 2:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/e83fab32d721034feabee8f1192bd2a9b8598e3b/drivers/flash/flash_stm32g4x.c#L192

I tried this out and it works. But it's interesting that I can still read out the written data at 0x08020000 from the previous tries using a debugger. So now I have the data in both locations. What would be the expected result if writing to a memory location that's physically not present (the discontinuity). I double-checked on my custom board, it's definitely an STM32G474RCT6. Same as @azeemshatp stated above.

Played around a bit more and I can confirm that `0x08020000` and `0x08040000` are not mapped to the same physical memory, as I can store different data which persists after reset. Seems like we get additional 256k flash for free if we ignore the `FLASH_SIZE` register ;)

Btw, the value of `FLASH_SIZE` register correctly reads `0x0100FFFF`, which means 256k.

Hi,
I don't want to modify `flash_pages_layout` as it is defined out of stm32 stuff,
so I tried a much more complex trick.
I push a branch in my fork (https://github.com/ABOSTM/zephyr.git):

* write to 0x08020000 should fail

> Seems like we get additional 256k flash for free if we ignore the FLASH_SIZE register ;)

I like the idea to create a large dummy flash page. Much cleaner than my quick hack. Are you creating a PR?

I am also gonna try this, and will update you how it went.
@azeemshatp: Yes, same issue here. `FLASH_PAGE_SIZE` is correctly set to 2048 (verified with printf), so there seems to be a bug somewhere in the validation.
